previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of psoriatic arthritis, diabetes, morbid obesity, and prior leg abscess was admitted for recurrent left calf swelling and spontaneous sanguinous drainage from a prior incision site. He had erythema, warmth, and ecchymosis but no fever or systemic signs of infection. Initial ultrasound showed a complex fluid collection without DVT. MRI revealed fluid tracking and mild myositis without abscess. Infectious disease recommended against antibiotics given stable vitals, normal labs, and no growth on blood cultures. The patient improved with conservative management, including pain control and continued immunosuppressive therapy. His blood sugars, initially over 400, were managed by increasing basal and prandial insulin. He was discharged home with optimized diabetes regimen, steroid taper adjustments, new antihypertensive, and follow-up planned with rheumatology.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old gentleman with past medical history of psoriatic 
arthritis, morbid obesity, Hypertension, diabetes type 2, MSSA 
abscess in the Left Lower Extremity requiring surgical 
intervention and fasciotomy (___ presented with 2 days 
history of bilateral lower extremity edema and exertional 
dyspnea.  
.  
# SOB & Lower extremity edema: There are several causes that 
might explain this. Most likely this was due to the higher total 
daily gabapentin dose for the last 6 days. His lower extremity 
bilateral swelling and 20 lb weight gain was noticed to be 
starting at the same time the dose of gabapentin was increased. 
On admission, his gabapentin dose was reduced to his prior 
regimen that is 800mg three times daily, since it can lead to 
lower limb swelling and edema. His new lower extremity bilateral 
edema and SOB was concerning of cardiac cause (right sided heart 
disease). His EKG, cardiac enzymes as well as echo were not 
suggestive cardiac cause. He had CTA in the ED which ruled out 
PE. He has been on steroids for a long time, which can also lead 
to fluid retention and lower limb edema. Hypoalbuminemia was 
considered, however his blood albumin level was normal. His TSH 
was within normal limits. He felt his breathing was doing better 
when he reached the medical floor from the ED. IV lasix was 
given twice on the floor with some improvement.
.  
# Lower extremity edema/erythema: He presented with new wide 
spread tender warm blanching erythema on his thighs mainly that 
is new for the patient. He also had petechiae like rash on his 
right leg. Previously he had MSSA abscess in his left leg that 
required surgical intervention and fasciotomy in ___. It 
was followed by recurrent fluid recollection that didn't grow 
organisms on cultures. It's unknown why he has been having this 
reccurency. On this admission, he was seen by rheumatology team 
for possible vasculitic process. They thought this is consistent 
with folliculitis (not petechiae) therefore no evidence of 
vasculitic like process. Dermatology was consulted as well who 
thought that the blanching erythema on the patient's lower 
extremities is consistent with inflammation secondary to 
swelling. There was no evidence of cellulitis which would be 
more demarcated, pink, and swollen. The fact that all of the 
petechiae are follicular argues against a vasculitic process. 
This is more of an irritant effect probably due to the swelling 
but some of it also appears to have been scratched. Clindamycin 
gel and compression stockings were recommended by dermatology 
team. Bilateral lower extremity venous US was negative for DVT.
.  
# Psoriatic arthritis: Not currently having acute exacerbation. 
Has used multiple regimens and currently on steroid taper. Has 
had swollen joints in the past. His dexamethasone was continued 
at the same dose as well as azathioprine. His prophylactic 
bactrim was also continued in addition to pain medications. 
.  
# Hypertension:

.  
# DM:  
- Continued his home glargine and was on insulin sliding scale. 
.  
# OSA: his CPAP was resumed while in hospital.
.  
# Osteoporosis: his home medications were continued.

PA AND LATERAL CHEST, ___ AT 1804 HOURS.

HISTORY:  Diabetes, hypertension, and dyspnea on exertion.

COMPARISON:  Multiple priors, the most recent dated ___.

FINDINGS:  The lungs are clear without consolidation or edema.  The
mediastinum is widened, but well defined.  The cardiac silhouette is within
normal limits accounting for patient and technical factors.  No effusion or
pneumothorax is noted.  The osseous structures are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:  Mediastinal widening is presumed secondary to lipomatosis.  The
lungs are clear without consolidation or edema.

INDICATION:  ___ man with psoriasis and obesity with acute shortness
of breath.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT images were acquired through the chest with and without IV
contrast.  The patient initally received 100 mL of optiray 350, however
pulmonary arterial opacifiaction was nondiagnostic.  The patient then received
an additional 70 mL of Optiray 350 and re-scanned yielding a diagnostic study.
Multiplanar reformations were obtained and reviewed.

CT OF THE CHEST WITH IV CONTRAST:

The thyroid gland is unremarkable.  There is no axillary or mediastinal
lymphadenopathy by CT size criteria.  The heart and great vessels are
unremarkable.  Note is made of mediastinal lipomatosis.  No pericardial
effusions are present.  The lungs show no nodules, effusions or
consolidations.  The airways and pulmonary arteries are patent down to the
subsegmental level.

Although this examination was not intended for subdiaphragmatic evaluation,
the partially imaged abdomen shows an aberrant left hepatic artery, likely
replaced.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:

The visible osseous structures show no suspicious lytic or blastic lesions or
fractures.

IMPRESSION:

1.  No acute intrathoracic process or pulmonary embolism.

2.  Mediastinal lipomatosis.

The need for IV hydration post-CT were communicated to the referring physician
___ via telephone at 10:30 pm on ___.
